ext.untrustedWorkspaces.description: It does not read files in the workspace. The Python path and the dashboard location can only be written to user settings, so the folder you have open can never swap out what actually runs.
ext.description: Opens Subagent Dashboard inside VSCode from any project — a screen that shows how Claude Code's subagents are moving as a family tree. The dashboard tool is bundled in, so this one extension is all it takes.

config.title: Subagent Dashboard
config.port.markdownDescription: The port to try first. If it is already in use, moves up to the next free port.
config.home.markdownDescription:
The path to the dashboard tool (where `dash.py` lives). Leave it empty to use `~/.claude/agent-dashboard`; if nothing is there, you will be asked whether to deploy the copy bundled with the extension.

This setting can only be written to user settings (so the folder you have open cannot swap out what gets run).
config.pythonPath.markdownDescription:
The Python executable to use. Leave it empty to search in this order: the interpreter selected in the Python extension → `python` → `py` → `python3`.

This setting can only be written to user settings.
config.openIn.description: Where "Open in a tab" displays it. When `agentDashboard.sidebarBehavior` is `openInTab`, opening from the activity bar icon follows this setting too.
config.openIn.enum.webview: Display embedded in a tab inside VSCode (default)
config.openIn.enum.simpleBrowser: Display in VSCode's bundled Simple Browser
config.openIn.enum.external: Display in the OS default browser
config.sidebarBehavior.markdownDescripti:
What happens when you press the activity bar icon.

With `openInTab`, the moment the sidebar opens it does the same thing as the "Open in a tab" command and closes the sidebar. VSCode has no way to replace what an icon click opens directly, so this works by opening it once and then moving it.

**Where it is shown follows `agentDashboard.openIn`.** If you have set that to `external`, pressing the icon opens the OS default browser instead.

When it cannot be opened, the sidebar is not closed; it shows the reason and the next step to take there instead.
config.sidebarBehavior.enum.openInTab: Move to a tab and close the sidebar (default)
config.sidebarBehavior.enum.embed: Display it as-is inside the sidebar
config.autoStartServer.description: When opening the screen, start the server automatically if it is not running.
config.showStatusBar.description: Show a Subagent Dashboard button in the status bar.
config.stopServerOnExit.markdownDescript: When VSCode closes, stop the server **that this extension started**. A server started elsewhere is left untouched.
config.runSetupOnFirstRun.markdownDescri:
The first time you use it, run the initial setup (`install.py`).

Installing the extension is taken to mean you intend to use it, so **this is not asked about — it just runs**, and you can see it happen in the progress notification and the message that follows. It writes how to use Subagent Dashboard into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (only the block between the markers) and makes `Ctrl+Shift+D` open it. Nothing outside your home directory is touched, and `python "install.py" --uninstall` undoes it. Once it has succeeded, it never runs again on its own (the "Run initial setup" command runs it any time). Turn this off if you do not want it to run by itself.
config.runChangelogSetupOnFirstRun.markd:
The first time you open a workspace (project folder), ask whether changelog tracking may be set up for it (`changelog_setup.py`).

This is separate from `agentDashboard.runSetupOnFirstRun`: it is asked once per workspace, not once per machine, because most people open more than one repository on the same machine. **It is never run without asking first**, and only the first folder of a multi-root workspace is offered automatically. Once it has succeeded (or been declined) for a workspace, it is never asked again there (you can still run it any time from the "Set up changelog tracking" command). The dialog also offers "Do not ask again in any workspace", which silences it everywhere at once. It is never offered for a folder that is not on the local file system (a virtual workspace) or for a workspace you have not trusted; the "Set up changelog tracking" command still works in a workspace you have not trusted.
config.autoUpdateOnNewVersion.markdownDe: When the extension is updated, ask whether to update `~/.claude/agent-dashboard` with the bundled tool. Records such as `missions/` are left untouched.
